name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.256.0 — /spec:plan's lock now runs decision-lint.js: a Decisions row that withholds a user affordance must carry [guards: <host § Risk Tiers text>] or [asked: <choice>], and a deferral row must cite a queue id spec-queue resolves; the plan ledger row records decisionLint counts. 7.255.0 — /spec:fix refuses to start on a dirty working tree: step 1 runs git status --porcelain first and STOPs naming the files, so one checkout carries one fix at a time and the gate, the reviewer and the fix row judge a single root cause. Fits the shipped read-load budget by tightening the intro and rules prose. 7.254.0 — New /spec:fix: the Direct lane's playbook for a defect repair wider than two layers or touching user-visible text — a root-cause statement before the first edit, one decisions stop over every authored string and policy choice, one different-family reviewer, then the host gate and /git:commit. No driver, no gate, no File Plan; core § Pipeline Entry points at it. The fleet reader knows the stage:"fix" row /git:commit now offers (sha, files, reviewed, via) so a later defect on those files is never attributed to the oldest spec that touched them.
